facts.text: Morphology: Kormendy (2019, arXiv:1810.10073): the Milky Way and its structural analogues are "giant, SBb - SBbc galaxies"; Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard (2016): "a luminous (L*) barred spiral", traditionally Sb-Sbc. The single string "SBbc" is the upper end of Kormendy's range, chosen so that it parses as a barred spiral; it is not a catalogue entry.
The Galaxy is a luminous barred spiral with a central box/peanut bulge, a dominant disc and a diffuse stellar halo.
The sky position given is that of the Galactic Centre (Sgr A*), the reference point of the structural model; the Sun is 8.178 kpc from it.

representation.summary: An analytic model assembled from cited literature: spiral arms are Reid et al. (2019) log-periodic fits to maser parallaxes; disc, bar and bulge parameters are the Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard (2016) recommended values. Only the Sun-Galactic-Centre distance is a direct geometric measurement; the far side and dust-obscured structure are model extrapolations, and no individual star is placed by this model.
exaggerations: Spiral arms are drawn as smooth curves of fixed width; real arms are irregular and partly extrapolated beyond the azimuth range of the maser data.

objects.notes: We live inside this galaxy; there is no external image of it. The model parameters are in models["milky-way"] (tables: spiral-arms-reid2019, spiral-arm-model-reid2019).

facts.text: The listed member galaxies are NOT a published membership list. Selection (ours): 2MASS Redshift Survey galaxies within 6 deg of M87 on the sky (about 1.7 Mpc projected radius at 16.5 Mpc) and with heliocentric cz between -500 and 2500 km/s. The window -500 to 2500 km/s is ours: it brackets the cluster's mean velocity (about 1100 km/s, with a velocity dispersion of order 600-700 km/s) roughly symmetrically, and it includes the blueshifted members that fall toward M87 (M86, M90, M98 have cz of order -100 to -250 km/s). It is still contaminated by foreground galaxies (low cz) and by background galaxies (W' cloud and beyond). It may contain foreground and background galaxies (a redshift cut cannot separate them from members; the survey of Mei et al. finds some Virgo-direction galaxies at ~23 Mpc in the W' cloud) and it misses members beyond the cone.

spiral-arm-model-reid2019.reference: Reid et al. 2019, ApJ 885, 131 (arXiv:1910.03357), sect. 3 and Table 2 notes

limitations: Spiral arms are log-periodic fits to ~200 maser parallaxes of high-mass star-forming regions (Reid et al. 2019); they describe the young, gas-rich tracers only, and the old stellar disc is not spiral in this model.

Arm centre lines are only constrained over the azimuth range betaMin..betaMax in the table; everywhere else (including most of the far side of the Galaxy, behind the Galactic Centre) the drawn arms are extrapolations of the fitted spiral, not observations.

In the fourth Galactic quadrant no maser parallaxes existed for the 2019 fits; arm positions there are constrained by tangency-longitude priors from CO and H I emission (Reid et al. 2019, Table 2 notes).

Dust extinction hides much of the disc and bulge from optical surveys; the far-side and obscured structure is inferred from infrared star counts, kinematics and models (Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016), and several parameters differ between methods.

Disc scale lengths and heights are described by the review itself as uncertain ("we are not able to present a fully consistent picture for the disk at this time"); the values here are the review's recommended means with its stated errors, not a fit to one data set.

Different parameters come from sources that assume different Sun-Galactic Centre distances (8.15 kpc Reid 2019, 8.2 kpc Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016, 8.178 kpc GRAVITY 2019); they are listed separately and not rescaled to a common value.
No warp, flare, or individual-star positions are included: drawing them would require data this model does not contain.
